text:
New Jersey comes in having won three straight, most recently 3-1 over Los Angeles on Saturday, with Anthony Mantha set to play his 600th NHL game. Dallas has won five in a row, the latest a 6-3 win over the Islanders on Sunday, and is doing it without Esa Lindell, Radek Faksa and Sam Steel. Joel Kiviranta has moved beside Mikko Rantanen and Wyatt Johnston in Steel's spot, and Arttu Hyry is up to 16:01 a night.

The Devils have been the better side by the numbers. They've taken 61% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five, against 54% for the Stars. Their 4-1 record in the last five understates it, since they out-chanced all five opponents. Our numbers say they are better than their record: a +4 goal difference on +13.7 expected, with finishing and goaltending costing them. Dallas has taken 4.1 penalties a game, which keeps handing out power plays. We have the Devils at 2.96 expected goals tonight and the Stars at 2.83.

In goal, projected starter Casey DeSmith (.925 this season, 9.74 goals saved above expected last year) replaces Jake Oettinger. New Jersey's goalie isn't confirmed. Arseny Gritsyuk has scored in five straight games, and as Mike Fink of The Hockey News posted, "It's Gritsyuk's fifth goal in as many games." We give Jack Hughes a 31% chance to score, while Johnston is at 37% and Jason Robertson 36% for Dallas.
